newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium's BBL launches euro-zone funds.
newsitem.headline: Belgium's BBL launches euro-zone funds.

text.p: Belgium's Banque Bruxelles Lambert SA launched on Friday two investment funds based, it said, on the countries it believes will take part in European economic and monetary union (EMU) from January 1, 1999.

The funds -- "BBL Invest Euro", for stocks, and "BBL Renta Fund Euro", for bonds -- will acquire assets originating in Germany, France, the Netherlands, Belgium and Luxembourg, Finland, Austria and Ireland.
"In launching these (funds), BBL offers investors the chance to already take part in the large euro zone," the bank said in a statement.

"The choice of countries could be adjusted in the future in case of variation of the composition of EMU," it added. The currency used in the funds would be the Ecus, while the euro could not be used as a currency for payments.
BBL said the funds would be issued in both income and growth shares. Growth shares would cost 250 Ecus. Income shares would cost 1,000 Ecus. The offer closes on March 21.
